title: Uneven token-priority handling caused regional 429 oscillations - action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-04 the API gateway began returning elevated 429 responses in a cyclical pattern across two regions (us-west-2 and eu-west-1). Traffic that should have been evenly rate-limited by token priority buckets instead observed oscillating enforcement: tokens alternating between permissive and strict enforcement windows every ~3-7 minutes. The symptom was a repeating burst of 429s for healthy customers followed by catch-up traffic, causing request spike churn, high client retries, and increased latency on downstream services. Impact: multiple high-volume customers experienced degraded user-facing latency and an increase in client-initiated backoffs for a ~5 hour window. No data loss or auth exposure was observed. This ticket captures the follow-up action items, verification steps, and engineering decisions to prevent recurrence.
postmortem_summary: Root cause: a race in the priority-mapping layer of the quota enforcer when combining dynamic overrides with regional sticky leases. The enforcer calculates per-token enforcement windows using (1) static quota rules, (2) dynamic per-customer priority overrides pushed from the control plane, and (3) a regional lease that pins a token to a controller for short intervals. A recent change (PR #14022) introduced a path where priority overrides were read from an eventual-cache without taking the same lease ordering as the enforcement windows. When the cache refresh and lease rotation aligned unfavorably, two controllers computed different enforcement windows for the same token, leading to alternating accept/reject patterns across regions. Contributing factors: insufficient test coverage for multi-controller lease races; lack of an end-to-end integration test simulating small lease windows; and brittle metrics that only surfaced aggregated 429 rates (not oscillation pattern).
root_cause: Priority override reads and lease rotations could be observed out-of-order across controllers because cache refresh path did not require lease sequencing. This allowed two controllers to compute conflicting enforcement state for the same token at overlapping times.
timeline: 2026-03-04 03:20 UTC - First customer alert: increased client retries and 429 spikes reported by Support.

2026-03-04 03:35 UTC - On-call ingested alerts. Initial mitigation: throttled automated retries via web-facing circuit-breaker, added temporary tenant-level soft-limit increases for affected customers.
2026-03-04 04:10 UTC - Engineering paged. Identified 429 oscillation pattern correlating with control-plane state refreshes and regional lease rotations.
2026-03-04 06:15 UTC - Deployed hotfix (rollback of PR #14022 cache path) to us-west-2; 429s reduced by ~80% in that region within 10 minutes.
2026-03-04 08:00 UTC - Coordinated global rollback and full mitigation complete. Incident declared resolved at 08:12 UTC.
2026-03-05 - Postmortem working session. Identified four actionable follow-ups and owners.
action_items: (Owner: Marco) Introduce lease-aware cache read: modify control-plane cache client to include lease sequence tokens and require monotonic ordering for priority override reads. Deliver PR and integration tests by 2026-03-18.

(Owner: Linh) Add an end-to-end integration test to the gateway CI that simulates two controllers with short (2-10s) lease rotations and dynamic priority override changes; validate deterministic enforcement convergence. Target CI merge by 2026-03-16.

(Owner: Ops) Expand metrics: add per-token enforcement-state metrics and a short-timescale oscillation detector (moving-window cross-region 429-correlation alert). Alert tuning and runbook updates by 2026-03-14.
(Owner: QA) Create a fuzz test harness for cache-control race scenarios focusing on eventual-consistency windows and bursty override changes; add to nightly regression suite by 2026-03-20.
(Owner: Security) Confirm no auth regression exposure; security review completed and documented in Confluence (link below). Due 2026-03-12.

(Owner: Product) Customer communication: draft a technical summary for affected customers explaining root cause, mitigation, and compensating controls; publish by 2026-03-15. Include recommended client backoff patterns.

(Owner: Infra) Short-term mitigation: implement a configurable minimum enforcement-stability window (default 15s) to reduce oscillation risk while work is underway; rollback toggle available. ETA 2026-03-12.
